manifest.source: Quest Spotlight on SQL Server (Spotlight Enterprise / Spotlight Cloud)
manifest.description: Mapping of Quest Spotlight on SQL Server alarm types to their nearest Redgate Monitor alert equivalents. Covers SQL Server alarms (87), Windows Server alarms (22), and Availability Group alarms (11). Each entry includes migration feasibility (direct/partial/custom/none/retire) and threshold conversion guidance.

severityMapping.strategy: Spotlight uses Low/Medium/High/Critical; Redgate Monitor uses Low/Medium/High. Critical and High both map to High in Redgate Monitor.

High.notes: Maps to High in Redgate Monitor

Informational.notes: Map to Low; consider retiring very noisy informational alarms

backup.daysToHours: Spotlight 'Days Since Last Full Backup' × 24 = Redgate Monitor hours threshold
backup.minutesToHours: Spotlight 'Minutes Since Last Log Backup' ÷ 60 = Redgate Monitor hours threshold
backup.hoursToHours: Spotlight 'Hours Since Last Differential Backup' = Redgate Monitor hours threshold (1:1)

memory.percentFreeToMbAvailable: Spotlight % Free Physical Memory: threshold_MB = total_RAM_MB × (spotlight_threshold_pct ÷ 100). Example: 20% free on 64 GB server → alert when available < 13107 MB
memory.physicalMbDirect: Spotlight 'Physical Memory Available (MB)' maps directly to Redgate Monitor OS memory available in MB

disk.percentUsedDirect: Spotlight 'Percentage Used' maps directly to Redgate Monitor Disk Used %
disk.percentFreeConvert: Spotlight % free → Redgate Monitor % used: 100 − spotlight_free_pct

blocking.secondsDirect: Spotlight blocking threshold is in seconds — same unit as Redgate Monitor. Direct threshold transfer.

logBackupMinutes.note: Spotlight 'Minutes Since Last Log Backup' ÷ 60 = Redgate Monitor hours. Recommended: 0.25 hours (15 min) for high-transaction systems, 1–4 hours for lower RPO requirements.

phases.name: Direct Replacements
phases.description: Spotlight alarms that map 1:1 to a built-in Redgate Monitor alert type with the same semantic meaning.
conditions: Locks - Blocked Processes → Blocking processes
Locks - Deadlocks → Deadlock (Extended Events)
Backup - Days Since Last Full Backup → Backup overdue
SQL - Long Running SQL → Long running query
SQL Agent - Jobs Failed → Job failing
Databases - Unavailable → SQL Server unavailable
CPU - Average CPU Usage → Processor (CPU) utilization
Memory - Physical Memory Available → OS memory available
Disks - Percentage Used / Free Space → Disk space
Disks - Transfer Time → Disk space / avg read-write time
I/O Stall Time → Disk space / avg read-write time
Network - Percentage Bandwidth → Network utilization
Availability Group - Failed Over → AG / Cluster failover
Clusters - Failed Over → AG / Cluster failover
Mirroring - Failedover → AG / Cluster failover
Tempdb File Size → Disk space
Databases - Data File Group Space Used → Disk space
Databases - Log File Space Used → Disk space

phases.name: Partial / Configured Replacements
phases.description: Spotlight alarms where a built-in Redgate Monitor alert covers the concept but has different behavior, different threshold units, or different granularity. Manual threshold adjustment or supplemental configuration required.
conditions: Backup - Hours Since Last Differential Backup → Backup overdue (type-filter needed)
Backup - Minutes Since Last Log Backup → Backup overdue (unit conversion: ÷60)
Clusters - Node Unavailable → AG / Cluster failover (node detail limited)
Clusters - Non-Preferred Node → AG / Cluster failover + custom DMV query
Memory - Percentage Free Virtual Memory → OS memory available (unit conversion)
Databases - Data File Group About to Grow → Disk space (reactive, not predictive)
Databases - SQL I/O Errors → SQL Server log entry (pattern match 823/824/825)
Error Log alarms → SQL Server log entry (keyword pattern matching only)
Mirroring - State → AG / Cluster failover (failover events only)
Log Shipping - Primary/Secondary Job → Job failing (job name filter needed)
SQL Agent - Status → SQL Server unavailable (proxy via Agent job monitoring)
SQL Agent - Long Running Jobs → Long running query (queries only, not Agent jobs)
Availability Group - Failover Availability → AG / Cluster failover (health not monitored)
Tempdb Auto Growth → Disk space + SQL Server log entry
Services - Service Not Running → SQL Server log entry (event-based only)
CPU - Individual CPU Usage → Processor (CPU) utilization (per-core not supported)

phases.name: Not Available — Cannot be Replicated
phases.description: Spotlight alarms that have no T-SQL equivalent or depend on proprietary Spotlight features / external products. Document as known gaps and address with alternative tooling.
conditions: Performance Investigator — Spotlight-proprietary composite score; no T-SQL equivalent
Poor Performance Health — Spotlight composite health score; use individual RG Monitor alerts
LiteSpeed Backup Failed/Warning — requires Quest LiteSpeed product
Clusters - File Share Witness Inaccessible — Windows cluster quorum resource (no T-SQL)
Tempdb File Location — configuration audit; enforce via build standards/DSC
Tempdb Growth Settings — configuration audit; enforce via build standards/DSC
Tempdb Number of Files — configuration audit; enforce via build standards/DSC
File - Exceeded Set Size — WMI file size monitoring; no T-SQL equivalent
Windows - Up Time — OS uptime; no T-SQL equivalent
Services - Power BI Reporting Service — PBIRS service not T-SQL accessible
Paging - File Collision — Windows paging configuration; enforce via OS policy
Monitored Server (SQL/Windows/AG) internal alarms — Spotlight internal health only
alternatives: LiteSpeed alarms: switch to native SQL Server backup monitoring via Backup overdue alert
File Share Witness: monitor via Windows cluster event logs (Event ID 1135/1177)
Tempdb config alarms: enforce correct configuration via PowerShell DSC or Group Policy Objects
Windows Up Time: monitor via Windows Event Log ID 6005/6006/6008 (startup/shutdown)
PBIRS service: monitor via Get-Service PowerShell remoting or SCOM/Nagios agent
Performance Investigator: use Redgate Monitor Dynamic Alerts (ML) in v14+ for composite anomaly detection

phases.description: Spotlight alarms that are Spotlight-internal health monitors. Redgate Monitor handles its own agent health internally — these should not be recreated.
